 'Rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi': Sanjay Raut's demand amid Dadar Metro renaming row

 Edited by Priyanka Mukherjee / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 21, 2026, 10:08 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print File photo of Sanjay Raut NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Friday demanded that Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar, amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'Chaityabhoomi'. Raut urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis to bring a proposal to rename Nagpur, saying his party would extend its support even if the move faced opposition. "Dadar is just a station. The biggest honour to Dr Ambedkar would be to change Nagpur's name to Deekshabhoomi. The chief minister should bring a proposal and we will support it," Raut told reporters. He said Deekshabhoomi held immense historical significance as the site where Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956, marking a turning point in the movement against caste discrimination. "Social revolution in Dr Ambedkar's life began at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. We will stand by the government on this if any conflict arises on the issue," he added. The demand also found support from the Congress, with legislature party leader Vijay Wadettiwar questioning why Nagpur could not be renamed after the historic site. "The name (of Nagpur) should be changed to Deekshabhoomi. What is the problem in changing the name to Deekshabhoomi?" Wadettiwar said. He credited Ambedkar with framing a Constitution that protects India's democracy and said Deekshabhoomi attracts visitors from across the world. The BJP, however, criticised Raut over his demand and accused Shiv Sena (UBT) of opposing the proposed renaming of Dadar Metro station. Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders were using the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) as a proxy to oppose the government's move. He said Raut should first welcome the decision to rename the Metro station as Chaityabhoomi. "He (Raut) never goes to Chaityabhoomi, nor does he propagate Dr Ambedkar's thoughts. Such people have no right to speak on the issue," Ban said. Maharashtra minister and senior BJP leader Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Nagpur was already widely associated with Deekshabhoomi. "Every person who comes to Nagpur goes to Deekshabhoomi," he said. This comes after Fadnavis announced the state government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station as Chaityabhoomi, subject to completion of the necessary procedures. The announcement had initially caused confusion over whether the proposed name change concerned Dadar railway station. The chief minister's Office subsequently clarified that the proposal applied only to the Metro station and that the suburban railway station would retain its existing name. Join conversation

 The renaming proposal has drawn political reactions, with the MNS raising objections to changing Dadar's name. Both Chaityabhoomi and Deekshabhoomi are closely associated with Ambedkar's life and legacy. On October 14, 1956, Ambedkar converted to Buddhism along with hundreds of thousands of followers at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. The event became a defining moment in the Dalit Buddhist movement. Ambedkar died on December 6, 1956, and was cremated at Chaityabhoomi in Mumbai's Dadar area. Both sites attract large numbers of followers every year, particularly during Dhammachakra Pravartan Din in Nagpur and Mahaparinirvan Diwas in Mumbai.
